notes:
Summary: large consumer ecommerce brand exploring tool-calling + agent assist. Primary goal: automate refunds and routing while keeping 99.95% ticket success under peak holiday loads.

Key quote from Head of CX: "We need automated refunds that are provably safe — no double-credits and auditable actions."

Shorthand from discovery calls: POC scope = refund orchestration (Stripe + internal ledger), ticket create/update in ServiceNow, escalation webhook to Ops Slack channel, idempotent tool-calls, structured output for audit. Want signed webhooks and per-call trace IDs.

Security: will insist on KMS integration for keys, HSM optional for on-prem, SOC2 + ISO27001 required. Data residency: EU/NA partitions depending on brand.

Pricing sensitivity: low-to-medium; willing to pay for guaranteed latency/SLA during Q4 spikes. Interested in Dedicated for throughput and Private for PCI-scoped refunds.

Communication notes: AE ran walkthrough of Redwood Console on 2026-02-15 (see ff_20260215_3b9a2c). SE follow-up to map current ServiceNow API workflows (ticket fields, custom actions). Procurement asked for sample contract with encryption clauses.

technical_requirements: Must support tool-calls to ServiceNow (REST), Stripe (refunds idempotent), internal ledger (gRPC) with per-request audit headers, signed JWT auth and KMS-backed keys. Requirement for request tracing: per-call trace_id passed back to Redwood logs. Latency target: 95th <= 300ms for agent-assist responses during normal load; durable throughput target 1500 rps for ticket create/update during spikes; graceful degradation strategy required (fallback to queued webhook + human-in-loop if model unavailable). Must provide model-level gating for PII redaction and allow customer-managed redaction hooks.
poc_plan: Week 1: Deploy Dedicated nodes in customer VPC, configure ServiceNow and Stripe test credentials
Week 2: Run synthetic spike test (3x baseline, 30s bursts) and measure latency/throughput
Week 3: Validate idempotent refund flow (edge-case: double refund prevention) and end-to-end audit logs
Week 4: Live shadowing with 500 real agent interactions + ticket summarization before go/no-go
recent_feedback: SE notes: initial tests show good batching behavior but need explicit KV cache tuning for long conversations. Customer flagged a preference for deterministic tool-call retries (exponential backoff + jitter) and explicit 'action-confirm' messages for agents. Procurement: wants sample SLA with 99.95% uptime and incident response times.
